newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:

AMLC COMMENTARY: Prices for cattle rose a little in the past week but eastern states lamb markets moved sharply lower.

Across Queensland, over the hooks quotes and auction prices for export steer categories ranged from firm to 10 cents/kg dearer. In the southern part of the state, average saleyard prices for steers suited to the Japanese market rose by about 5 c/kg while steers of Korean specifications rose by a slightly lesser amount. Cow prices improved again during the week, with medium weight score three cows selling on average for 153 cents/kg in the south.
Similar conditions applied in New South Wales and Victoria.
Markets for export cattle are being driven by lower supplies out of Queensland and by improving market conditions in North Asia.
Cattle slaughter in Queensland last week was 48,020 head, up five percent on the previous week but still well below the kill of 63,270 head in the same period of last year.
Further signs emerged this week of improved demand for Australian beef from North Asia.

For the second successive tender, results were favourable for Australia in the Korean tender awarded on September 13. Australian exporters secured 98 per cent or 1,728 tonnes of the grassfed fullsets awarded, with New Zealand taking the other two percent. Australian exporters also gained 86.8 percent or 4,350 tonnes of the grassfed quarter beef awarded, with the remainder going to New Zealand. Prices were up, particularly for fullsets, which gained on average 28 c/kg compared with the previous tender. Grassfed quarter beef prices were on average about five c/kg higher.

With the latest tender the Korean government has fulfilled its minimum GATT beef purchasing commitment for the 1996 quota year. Buying from Korea has made a contribution to the modest recovery in cattle prices in the past six weeks.

The market fior chilled beef to Japan also improved. Japanese wholesale prices for Australian chilled grassfed beef rose by more than 50 yen/kg for most product categories, while export prices were 5c-20c/kg higher. Since Aughust 23 export prices for chilled fullsets have risen by 53 c/kg.

But the trade to Japan is relatively lkow. Unless these levels pick up very consideravbley over the next 10 days, exports to Japan for September will be no more than the 18,800 tonnes recorded in August. In September 1995, 25,900 tonnes of beef were shipped to Japan. Beef demand in Japan, although improving, has yet to fully recover from the E.coli problems.
Prices of frozen beef to Japan have yet to display any real signs of improvement.
In the U.S., heavier placements of cattle into U.S. feedlots in July and August should start emerging from feedlots from about mid-November.
Eastern lamb markets tumbled this week with price falls of about 25-50 c/kg not uncommon. A primary factor is increased supplies
